text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: elevated 5xx rate on /v1/stream for hosted API during SDK 0.12 rollout canary. Alerting on-call.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: canary-tag=service-api:release-2025-04-01-0.12, cohort=10% (asia-north1). Trigger: sdk-client v0.12 auto-upgrade.

ana: paging @ana (oncall) — I'm seeing multiple customers reporting dropped stream events. Quick check: dashboard shows 5xx spike starting 2025-04-01T14:02:03Z.

ana: @mike can you confirm if any runtime changes were deployed with the release?

mike: I pushed the release that enables support for a new streaming framing (jsonlines) in the SDK, but server-side should be backwards-compatible. Canary was set to 10%.

mike: looking at logs:
```
2025-04-01T14:02:08Z service-api pod-47f2 ERR stream_parser.go:87 invalid event framing: unexpected token '\u0000'
2025-04-01T14:02:09Z service-api pod-47f2 WARN dropping connection, client=10.3.2.45
```

ana: that looks like framing mismatch. Joel, any support tickets yet?

joel: Support has 3 customers flagged (Acme, NovaPayment, ClefAnalytics) — they all reported streams either immediately disconnecting or never receiving events. I've put notes in the tickets and told them we're investigating.

mike: I suspect the SDK changed to emit chunked JSON-lines instead of SSE-like events by default when `stream: true` is set. Server still expects SSE framing (events with `data:` lines). Canary clients sent different framing -> parser fails.

tanya: Can we flip a kill-switch feature flag before rolling back the binary? Which flag controls server framing acceptance?

mike: There's a server flag `accept_jsonlines_streams` behind runtime config, default false. I see it wasn't set on the canary nodes. I am enabling it on canary now to test.

mike: `curl -v -N "https://canary.api.redwood/v1/stream?model=gpt-micro" -H "Authorization: Bearer ****"`
Response: HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< but then parser error in logs, client receives nothing.

ana: If enabling the server flag isn't quick enough, we should rollback the canary and disable auto-upgrade for SDK.

mike: Enabling flag on canary succeeded but we still see intermittent disconnects. Policy: kill canary rollout, rollback image to `release-2025-03-28-0.11`.

deploy-bot: Rolling back deployment: `kubectl -n api set image deployment/service-api service-api=service-api:release-2025-03-28-0.11 --record`

mike: Started rollback but noticed two pods failing to pull image on a dedicated node due to expired registry token. Pull errors: `rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to pull and unpack image` — working with infra to fix.

ana: @tanya I'm handing this over to you for the on-call shift — I'm going to lunch in ~10. Please coordinate the remaining mitigation and customer comms.

tanya: taking over. On infra token issue: @eng-infra, can you rotate the node pull secret for cluster api-prod-canary?

support-bot: Notifying affected customers: Acme (prod), NovaPayment (staging), ClefAnalytics (prod). Sending status update template.

eng-infra: rotated pull secret and restarted failing nodes: `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/registry-creds -n kube-system` — images now pulling.

mike: rollback to 0.11 completed on remaining replicas. Monitoring: 5xx rate dropping from 12% to 1.2% over the last 12 minutes.

joel: Notified customers via support with ETA and mitigation steps: recommended temporary pin to SDK v0.11 for stable streams and shared a short script to pin package.json.

joel: sent suggested customer message: "We're rolling back the recent SDK-related change causing streaming disconnects. If you pinned to v0.11 you'll be unaffected; otherwise we recommend downgrading until we ship a compatible fix. We'll follow up with timeline."

mike: Root cause summary so far: v0.12 SDK changed default streaming framing to jsonlines. Server parser wasn't toggled to accept jsonlines in all rollout nodes; canary clients triggered parser errors leading to dropped connections. Secondary issue: image pull failures delayed rollback on a subset of nodes.

tanya: Impact: Hosted API customers on auto-upgrade and in canary cohort experienced temporary stream loss. Dedicated/private deployments unaffected unless they pulled v0.12 server override. No data loss reported, but degraded user experience for 3 named customers and some ephemeral client retries.

tanya: Immediate actions:
- kill canary (done) and rollback (done)
- disable SDK auto-upgrade flag in control plane for SDK v0.12 rollout
- notify support & customers (joel done)
- open postmortem and assign owner (mike)

mike: Postmortem I'll own. Immediate dev tasks: revert SDK default to SSE framing, or make server accept jsonlines by default and add an `Accepts: application/x-sse` header check. Also add contract tests (client<->server streaming e2e).

ana: Add follow-up: enforce smoke canary smoke tests that exercise actual streaming end-to-end (not just healthcheck). Create a 'streaming-contract' check that runs before canary rollout completes.

tanya: On-call handoff note: ana -> tanya at 14:12 UTC. If anything flares up, page `sre@redwood` and escalate to CTO.

support-bot: Creating incident ticket INC-2025-042: title "SDK 0.12 streaming framing incompatibility — canary rollback" and linking customer tickets.

mike: Monitoring shows stability for 10+ minutes now. I'll keep an eye on logs and open the postmortem doc.

tanya: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a brief status update to #general and the postmortem link when it's ready. :white_check_mark:
